title: Find the cheapest McDonald's China order with coupons
summary: Developer hujjun's WorkBuddy skill gathers McDonald's China menus and coupons to find the cheapest order; the author reports a ¥47 Big Mac meal dropping to ¥21.90 in sample data.
agent_role: The agent interprets the request, queries stores, menus, four coupon sources and nutrition data, normalizes it, calls the optimizer, explains the options and creates the order. The user confirms before ordering.
outcome: Author reports a Big Mac meal priced ¥47 drops to ¥21.90 (53% off) in the sample data, and notes that real-account testing showed coupons must be pulled from four sources to find the best combo.
what_they_did: Developer hujjun built a skill for the WorkBuddy agent for a McDonald's developer contest, using a connector to McDonald's China's ordering system. When a user asks for the cheapest way to order, the agent gathers stores, menu, prices, nutrition and coupons from four sources. A fixed Python program then works out the cheapest valid combination. The price is rechecked and the user confirms before the order is created.
how_it_went: On sample data, the author reports a Big Mac, medium fries and Coke drop from ¥47.00 to ¥21.90, a 53% saving, using a 1+1 combo coupon. They note the sample prices and coupons are demo snapshots, so real prices depend on the store.
worth_knowing: Testing with a real account, the author found one coupon source misses the best deal: some coupons must be claimed first, some are store-only, and some work only for pickup. The math is left to code because AI models often get prices and discounts wrong.
prompt: I want to order [items] from [restaurant] near [your location], for [pickup/delivery], with a budget of [amount] and up to [calorie limit]. Use the restaurant's ordering tools to fetch the menu, prices and every available coupon, including ones I can claim but haven't yet. Do the price math in code, not in your head. Respect each coupon's stacking rules and channel limits, and include delivery fees. Show me the top 3 cheapest valid combinations with their totals and the coupons used. Re-check the final price, and wait for my confirmation before you place any order or start payment.

curation.rationale: A clear, reproducible daily-life agent workflow that fetches live menu and coupon data, runs a deterministic optimizer and places orders after confirmation, with code and self-tests; the headline 53% saving is computed on sample snapshot data and it is a contest entry.
